 Judgment

M.F.A No.202171/2017 is filed by the insurer challenging the quantum of compensation and the liability fastened on it to pay the compensation determined by the II Additional District and Sessions Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bidar, sitting at Basavakalyan,
(henceforth referred to as 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.663/2015 by its Judgment and award dated 10.07.2017.
2.

entities.text: II Additional District and Sessions Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bidar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: M.F.A. No.201162/2018 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal in MVC No.663/2015.
3. The appellant in MFA No.202171/2017 who is arrayed as respondent No.2 in MFA No.201162/2018 shall henceforth be referred to as the 'insurer' of the autorickshaw involved in the accident.
The appellant in MFA No.201162/2018, who is respondent No.1 in MFA No.202171/2017 shall henceforth be referred to as the 'claimant'.
Respondent No.2 in MFA No.202171/2017 who is arrayed as respondent No.1 in MFA No.201162/2018 shall henceforth be referred to as the 'owner' of the autorickshaw involved in the accident.

4. The impugned judgment and award discloses that the claimant, a 5 year old boy, met with an accident on 13.08.2015 involving an autorickshaw bearing registration No.AAT-1503 (henceforth The Manager vs Md. Zaid And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188865661/
3 referred to as 'the vehicle in question').

entities.text: Manager vs Md. Zaid And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The claimant suffered injuries and therefore, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, 'the Act') claiming compensation of Rs.6,00,000/- from the owner and insurer of the vehicle in question.
5.

The Tribunal after considering the oral and documentary evidence, awarded compensation of a sum of Rs.1,22,300/- to the claimant and directed the insurer to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realization.

6. Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal and the liability fastened on it to pay the compensation, the insurer has filed M.F.A No.202171/2017 and the injured claimant has preferred MFA No.201162/2018 seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

7. Learned counsel for the insurer submitted that the vehicle in question did not carry a permit and therefore, there was violation of conditions of policy of insurance and hence, the insurer was exonerated from its liability to pay the compensation.
8. Learned counsel for the claimant submitted that the claimant had suffered fracture of left tibia and fibula at middle and lower 1/3rd junction.
Therefore, the compensation determined by the Tribunal was inadequate and warranted enhancement.

9. This Court in terms of the order dated 14.02.2023 had adjourned the appeals to 01.03.2023 in order to enable the learned counsel for the claimant to produce copy of the permit that the vehicle in question carried so as to determine the question whether the insurer was liable to pay the compensation determined by the Tribunal.

Learned counsel for the claimant submits that the claimant is not in a position to secure the permit in respect of the vehicle in question and that the owner of the vehicle in question though served with the notice/s of these appeals, has failed to appear before the Court.

10. Learned counsel for the claimant further submits that the compensation of Rs.1,22,300/- is awarded by the Tribunal considering the notional income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.15,000/-
per annum.

He submits that the Tribunal has taken functional disability at 5% while the injury was to the tibia and fibula, both the bones of the left leg of the claimant and therefore, the Tribunal ought to have assessed the disability at not less than 15%.
11. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the insurer as well as the learned counsel for the claimant.
I have perused the records of the Tribunal and its judgment and award.
12. The accident is not in dispute and the resultant injury suffered by the claimant is also not in dispute.
The claimant was aged 5 years at the time of the accident.

Having regard to the fact that the claimant had suffered fracture of both the bones of his left leg, it was appropriate that the Tribunal ought to have considered the disability suffered by him at 10% as against the evidence of PW.2 that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 20% to the whole body.

Having regard to the age The Manager vs Md. Zaid And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188865661/
4 of the claimant at the time of the accident and the physical disability suffered by him, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced as follows:
 Sl. Heads of Compensation Amount  No. (In Rupees)
 1. Pain and suffering 30,000/-
 2. Medical expenses 73,800/-
 3. Loss of amenities 30,000/-
 4. Attendant charges, 30,000/-
 nourishing food etc.
 5. Loss of income due to 27,000/-
 disability  (Rs.15,000/- x 10% x 18)
 TOTAL 1,60,800/-
13.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In so far as the contention of the insurer that the vehicle in question was not carrying a permit, in view of the law declared by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Amrit Paul Singh and another v.
Tata AIG General Ins. Co. Ltd. and others1 and the judgment of the Full Bench of this Court in the case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Yallavva and another2, the insurer cannot avoid liability to pay the compensation and that it is entitled to recover it as provided therein.
2018 ACJ 1768 ILR 2020 Kar 2239 14. In view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex court in Amrit Paul Singh (supra), the appeal in MFA No.202171/2017 filed by the insurer is allowed in part and the insurer is directed to pay the enhanced compensation of Rs.38,500/- to the respondent No.1/claimant along with interest at 6%
per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of payment, excluding interest for the delayed period of 242 days in filing the appeal in MFA No.201162/2018 by the respondent No.1.
15.

sentences.text: The appellant/insurer is entitled to recover the compensation and interest from respondent No.2, the owner of the offending vehicle by executing this judgment in accordance with law.
16. The amount, if any, in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal.
17. Therefore, the appeal in MFA No.201162/2018 filed by the claimant is also allowed in part.
The compensation of Rs.1,22,300/- awarded by the Tribunal to the claimant in MVC No.663/2015 is enhanced to Rs.1,60,800/-.

The enhanced compensation of Rs.38,500/- is payable by the insurer with interest at 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till - 10 - the date of payment, excluding interest for the delayed period of 242 days in filing this appeal.
